name: Clarivax
description: Clarivax is a fast-acting, short-duration anxiolytic specifically engineered for BCI-integrated users experiencing neural-input anxiety — the specific panic response triggered by information overload, interface saturation, or sensory flood from always-on connectivity. Where Pacitrel is the chronic daily maintenance drug, Clarivax is the acute rescue dose, working within minutes to quiet the neural noise and restore a functional emotional baseline. Nightshade sells it legally but its gray-market versions are far more concentrated.
effects: Specific quieting of BCI-mediated stress responses
Reduced sensory overwhelm and information-processing panic
Restoration of emotional baseline without sedation
Brief window of unusual mental clarity as anxiety lifts
side_effects: Rebound anxiety spike 30-60 minutes after dose ends if underlying stressor persists
Gray-market concentrated versions cause dissociation at high doses
Frequent use blunts the anxiety signals that warn of genuine BCI system threats
Interaction with certain BCI firmware versions can cause temporary interface blackout
Psychological dependency develops rapidly due to fast-acting relief profile
Users who take it before important decisions may underweight legitimate risk signals
street_price: Φ30 per dose (gray market Φ15 for concentrated version)
cultural_context: Clarivax fills the gap between Pacitrel's slow chronic action and the acute panic attacks that GLMZ's constant neural connectivity produces. In Tier 1 and 2, where BCI systems are often older, noisier, and less well-maintained, neural anxiety spikes are more frequent and more severe. Clarivax is the drug you take when your interface is screaming and you still have four hours of shift left. The concentrated gray-market version, called 'the open,' is technically illegal but so widely used in the Gray Zone that enforcement is selective at best.
story_hooks: A the Gray Zone runner discovers that their increasingly frequent Clarivax use is not just managing anxiety — their BCI is actually malfunctioning in a way that mimics anxiety, and the drug has been masking a hardware fault that could kill them

Nightshade's legal Clarivax and its gray-market concentrated version turn out to share a supply chain — someone inside Nightshade is diverting pharmaceutical-grade compound to unlicensed the Gray Zone labs and taking a cut

A BCI technician realizes that a recent firmware update pushed by a major corp deliberately increases neural noise in users who are behind on their subscription payments — essentially manufacturing the anxiety that Clarivax treats
